season.evidence: Stored Jul-Sep. Peakbagger successful ascents: Jun 94, Jul 72, Aug 60, Sep 64, Oct 100 (larch season). Web search of Mountaineers/WTA reports: mid-June still has snow and a frozen Lake Ingalls needing an ice axe above the lake; July-Aug snow-free approach; early/mid-October reports found snow and ice on the scramble. Oct is usable but riskier.

facts.text: Mid-June: snow bridges over running water in the basin below the col can give way when probed; Lake Ingalls is still partly frozen.
Ice axe, microspikes and helmet (mid-June snowfields to the col)
Mid-October: a skiff of fresh snow ices the slabs, upper trail and summit blocks; the face right of the col becomes unsafe.
Traction spikes for the upper trail near the pass (mid-October)
Near the top, the gully left of the summit works well, and keeping to the north side of the summit block makes the final pitch nearly a walk (June-August).
The steep dusty climbers' path from the col is slick and a snow patch can linger across it into August; boulders beside it grip better than the dust.
After the col, you pass a lichen-covered knob that needs the pack off to squeeze through a narrow gap before the easier slope to the top.

notes: Stored season Jul-Sep is narrower than ascent history; Oct has 100 logged ascents but conditions are weather-dependent. The catalog holds a single row for this peak although other roped lines exist on Ingalls.
